post.instagram_caption:
Does one AI prompt really use a whole bottle of water? Not by today's best numbers.

The viral claim came from a UC Riverside study shared by The Washington Post in 2024: generating 100 words with GPT-4 was estimated at 235 ml of water in Texas and over 1,400 ml in Washington. In 2025 Google published its own measurement: a median Gemini text prompt uses about 0.26 ml, roughly five drops. OpenAI's Sam Altman says an average ChatGPT query uses about one fifteenth of a teaspoon.

The catch: these are the companies' own numbers. Google's figure counts only data center cooling water, covers text prompts only, and long reasoning tasks likely use more.

The lesson: one prompt is tiny, but at global scale small numbers add up.

Source: MIT Technology Review, Aug 21, 2025, and Google's paper.

post.youtube_description:
A viral 2024 estimate from UC Riverside, shared by The Washington Post, said generating 100 words with GPT-4 could use 235 ml to over 1,400 ml of water, depending on the data center. In 2025 Google measured a median Gemini text prompt at about 0.26 ml, roughly five drops, and OpenAI's Sam Altman claims about one fifteenth of a teaspoon per ChatGPT query. These are company figures: Google's counts only data center cooling water and text prompts.

Sources:
• MIT Technology Review, "In a first, Google has released data on how much energy an AI prompt uses" (Aug 21, 2025)
• Google, "Measuring the environmental impact of delivering AI at Google Scale" (arXiv, Aug 2025)
• Tom's Hardware, "Using GPT-4 to generate 100 words consumes up to 3 bottles of water" (Sep 19, 2024)
• TechRadar, "Sam Altman thinks ChatGPT's energy usage is nothing to worry about" (Jun 2025)
